bulletins.title: CDT-Bulletin Reader Requests 'Bridgerton-style' reporting on the events so far
bulletins.summary: The Briefing, the Confirmation, the Ethics and the Placements, retold for the Season by the Editors, with names changed to protect the guilty.
bulletins.body:
Dearest gentle reader, the Season is well underway and the drawing room of the Briefing was, by all accounts, rather sparsely attended. Your humble author has gathered the whispers of three most talked-about announcements and presents them here, in the manner society demands.

THE MATTER OF THE CONFIRMATION

Lord Aldridge, a gentleman of considerable standing at the Centre, caused no small flutter amongst the Second Season by declaring that the eighteenth month is the happy target, while the twenty-fourth is understood to be the outer limit of all patience. Those who fail to be confirmed by then may, depending on the customs of each great house, depart with the lesser honour of an MPhil. One does so hate to dwell on such things.

Lady Penhallow, ever the one to speak plainly, was heard to suggest that at the Royal House of Holloway the eighteenth month may be treated with rather more severity than at Surrey. A young gentleman of Surrey countered that both the written Report and the Viva are meant to be concluded around that same month.

The Dowager Lady Carlisle, a figure whom all agree is quite legendary, promised that further word on the Confirmation shall be sent post-Briefing, and that a panel of examiners shall be consulted with supervisors. Lady Sylvaine of Surrey added, with a flourish of her fan, that Surrey's own are expected to attend a compulsory session at the Doctoral College beforehand.

Your author confesses that this preamble might have been better delivered before the occasion, with particulars for each house. A brisk recapitulation and some time for questions would have sufficed. Still, one must give the researchers and academics some reason to leave their country estates and attend the office.

THE MATTER OF THE ETHICS

Lady Penhallow then turned to the weighty subject of ethics applications, for those who have not yet submitted and received their sign-off, and promised a workshop to assist the afflicted. It is said that the application and the training portfolio shall be due at the twelfth month, beginning with the Third Season. Those of earlier Seasons who have yet to submit shall be advised in due course. Whether that course is due soon, none can say.

THE MATTER OF THE PLACEMENTS

Lord Aldridge next addressed the question of placements, though whether for the First, Second or Third Season was not wholly clear amidst a confusion of numerals and slides. Such are the trials of our modern age.

To measure the appetite of the room, his lordship conducted a rapid and entirely informal poll of those present. Your author, attempting to read the mood, observed that perhaps fifty to sixty per cent raised their hands with a breezy indifference as to whether the Centre had any say in the matter. We eagerly await further polling of such refined and binary opinion.

A placement would ideally be announced six months before one takes leave. A single month is likely the least notice the Centre would tolerate, though one is advised to take the lead of one's supervisor. Placements are advised between the twenty-fourth and forty-eighth month, and some manner of formal agreement shall be put in place.

Two kinds of placement were laid out. The first, the Integral placement, is open to all and aligned with the doctorate, potentially with partners in industry. Funding, registration and completion are not paused, which some may find a hard bargain. The second, the Non-Integral placement, is with a partner beyond the Centre, and funding and registration are paused whilst one goes off to seek one's fortune.

A delicate dispute over intellectual property was hinted at when the Integral placement was discussed, with the Centre's branding present in every corner. For Non-Integral placements, the traditional path applies, in which the company owns the work. One may imagine the exchange. The Centre: "We should like to own all the intellectual property, if you please." The Company: "I beg your pardon?"

Your author reminds the reader that these accounts are the whispers of a drawing room, and not the word of the registry. Please consult the official rules before arranging your life accordingly.

Yours, as ever, The Editors

bulletins.title: Adrian outlines details on placements for Cohort 1, or is it Cohort 2? Or 3?
bulletins.summary: Numeric confusion and powerpoint challenges continue to be rife in the Age in AI.
bulletins.body:
To gauge the appetite of CDT researchers wanting to do a placement as part of the PhD, Adrian conducts a rapid "trust me bro" poll with members of the audience present at the briefing.

CDT Editors attempted to get the vibe and can confidently say it felt like 50-60% put their hands in the air like they just don't care whether the CDT has any say in them pursuing a placement or not. We look forward to more polls to help understand the binary opinions smart people in a room.

Taking a placement would "ideally" be notified six-months ahead of taking leave. 1-month is likely the minimum notice period CDT would be happy with, but take lead from your supervisor.

Placements are advised to be taken between month-24 to 48 and CDT have to put in place some sort of formal agreement, in order for the placement to be taken.

Adrian outlines two possible placements:

1. Integral placements (open to all). Working on something aligned with the PhD, potentially challenge-industry partners, PhD funding is not paused not is PhD regirstation and completion... tough sell for some.

2. Non-integral placements. Non-CDT partners, PhD funding and registration paused (aka BYE SEE YOU IN A FEW MONTHS WHILE I EARN BIG DOLLAR $$$$$).

Tricky IP negotiations might arise hinted while outlining the integral placement option. CDT riddled throughout, ensuring you are completely branded head-to-toe.

Non-CDT placements follow "traditional" PhD route: company owned:

CDT: "we would like to own all the IP please, for all the CDT researcher's efforts while with you on placement".

Company: "u wot m8?"

bulletins.title: Adrian invokes fear amongst Cohort 2 with Confirmation Viva Timeline.
bulletins.summary: Adrian reportedly highlights that month-18 is the target, while month-24 is understood to be the outer limit. Not passing by then may, depending on the regulations at each institution, mean graduating with an MPhil instead. Check the official rules.
bulletins.body:
Polly seems to suggest that at Royal Holloway, month-18 may be treated as a harder deadline than at Surrey.

A Surrey CDT researcher understands that both the written Confirmation Report and the Viva are meant to be completed around month-18.

The legendary Carolina says it how it is: she will be sending out more confirmation info post briefing. Panel of examiners will be consulted with supervisors as part of the process.

Sylwia jumps on the  bandwagon by adding: "Surrey researchers have to complete a compulsory/mandatory doctoral college session on preparing for the confirmation process".

CDT Brief editors believe that this preamble information could of been better explained prior to today's session, especially with specifics for both institutions and the process. The briefing could of been a quick recap/overview with additional question handling. However, CDT researchers and academics need some reason to come to the office right?

bulletins.title: Cohort 3 not in briefing, lucky them.
bulletins.summary: Sylwia warms up for Adrian who claims CDT researchers are "always important to us". Editors of the CDT Brief wonder if this hints toward a retrospective stipend update to prior cohorts.... yeah right.
